paper.title: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential

result.summary: 本文介绍了 Orb，一个用于材料原子建模的通用原子间势函数家族 [abstract]。Orb 采用可扩展的图神经网络架构，从数据中学习原子相互作用的复杂性，而不依赖旋转等变性等架构约束 [S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1]。模型训练分为扩散预训练和监督学习两个阶段 [S2.SS3.p1]。在 Matbench Discovery 基准上，Orb 发布时相比其他方法误差降低 31%，并且比现有通用势函数快 3-6 倍 [abstract]。作者还评估了 Orb 在几何优化、蒙特卡洛和分子动力学模拟中的表现 [abstract]。

research_question.text: 本文旨在开发通用原子间势函数，以解决现有势函数通常局限于小系统且难以跨材料类别泛化的问题 [S4.p1]。作者关注如何利用可扩展的图神经网络架构，从数据中学习原子相互作用的复杂性及其不变性，而非使用架构上受约束的模型 [S1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1]。

evidence.quote: Generally, these interatomic potentials have been confined to a small system domain and struggled to generalize across different material classes.

Our key innovation in Orb is to adapt this approach to materials modeling, focusing on a scalable graph neural network architecture which learns the complexity of atomic interactions and their invariances from data, rather than using architecturally constrained models which respect rotational equivariance or particular group symmetries.

method.text: Orb 的核心是一个图网络模拟器（GNS），并增强了平滑图注意力机制，节点间的消息基于注意力权重和距离截断函数更新 [S2.p1]。模型训练分为两个阶段：首先使用基态材料数据集训练去噪扩散模型，然后以此初始化神经网络势，以监督方式预测能量、力和应力 [S2.SS3.p1]。

evidence.quote: The backbone of Orb is a Graph Network Simulator (GNS) augmented with a smoothed graph attention mechanism, where messages between nodes are updated based on both attention weights and distance-based cutoff functions.
Orb models are trained in two distinct phases - first they are trained as Denoising Diffusion models using a dataset of ground state materials.
Secondly, the base models are used to initialize a Neural Network Potential which predicts the energy, forces and stress of systems and is trained in a supervised manner.

experiments.text: 作者在 Matbench Discovery 基准上评估了 Orb，并与现有方法进行了比较 [S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1]。速度基准测试在单个 NVIDIA A100 GPU 上进行，比较了 Orb 与 MACE 的前向传播速度 [S3.F3]。此外，还在 MD17-10k 数据集上进行了零样本评估，测试模型从零温周期性晶体结构泛化到未见高温非周期性分子的能力 [S3.SS4.SSSx2.p1]。

evidence.quote: The full results, accurate as of the time of submission (2024-10-14), are in Table 1.
left: Model forward pass speed (excluding featurization) compared to MACE on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU.
Such a zero-shot evaluation is quite ambitious; ow well can models trained on zero-kelvin periodic crystal structures generalize to unseen high-temperature non-periodic molecules ?

findings.text: 在 Matbench Discovery 基准上，Orb 模型在主要指标 F1 上设定了新的 state-of-the-art，并在其他指标上普遍更优，尤其具有高精度 [S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1]。Orb 模型比 MACE 快 3 到 6 倍（大系统尺寸下）[S3.F3]。在 MD17-10k 零样本评估中，Orb (MPtraj) 表现最佳，h(r) 更低，甚至优于许多分子特异性基线 [S3.SS4.SSSx2.Px1.p1]。此外，Orb 在模拟中表现出优异的稳定性，所有分子均达到最大 300ps [S3.SS4.SSSx1.Px1.p1]。

evidence.quote: For both sections, Orb models set a new state-of-the art across the primary metric (F1), and are generally superior across other metrics.

Orb models have especially high precision, which would likely be crucial in a real-world use-case where false-positives (i.e. materials that are predicted as stable but are not) are very costly due to wasted experimental effort.
At large system sizes, Orb is between 3 to 6 times faster than MACE.
Comparing just those models trained on MPtraj, we see that Orb has the best performance, with a lower $h(r)$ across the board.
It is noteworthy that Orb (MPtraj) outperforms many of the molecule-specific baselines in Table 2, and is not far from matching the molecule-specific versions of Orb.
Orb demonstrates excellent stability, achieving the maximum 300ps for all molecules, putting it on par with NequIP and ahead of all other baseline models.

limitations.text: 作者指出，在 MD17-10k 零样本评估中，所有模型性能相当接近，从四个模拟的样本量难以稳健判断优越性；添加 Alexandria 到训练集反而降低性能的结果可能在大样本中不具统计显著性 [S3.SS4.SSSx2.Px2.p1]。此外，Orb 是非保守的，直接预测力而非能量梯度，需要净扭矩移除等操作来确保力的理想性质 [S3.SS4.SSSx2.Px4.p1]。作者还提到，OMAT24 数据集上训练的 EquiformerV2 模型在 Matbench Discovery 上超越了 Orb-v2 [S6.SS6.p1]。

evidence.quote: Whilst Orb (MPtraj) does outperform MACE and Sevennet (Table 3), all models are reasonably close in performance and it is hard to make a robust judgement of superiority from a sample size of four simulations.
Indeed, the somewhat surprising result that adding in Alexandria to Orb’s training set lowers performance may not be statistically significant across a larger sample of molecules.

The need for this operation—as well as the ‘mean removal’ operation also described in Section 6.3 —arises from the fact that Orb is non-conservative i.e. it directly predicts forces rather than computing the gradient of an energy function.
EquiformerV2 models trained on this dataset surpass the performance of Orb-v2 on the Matbench Discovery benchmark.
